script: セイバールート十五日目-11
title: セイバールート十五日目-11

pages.ja:
月が遠い。
雲は晴れ、夜の闇は青みを帯びる。
じき黎明。
長かった夜は、これで終わろうとしていた。

pages.en:
—The moon is distant.

The clouds have cleared, and the darkness of night is tinged with blue.

Dawn will come soon.

The long night is finally drawing to its end.

pages.ja:
それが最後。
闇夜を越えて、セイバーと共に、この場所に辿り着いた。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
—This is the end.

Saber and I have crossed through the night to reach it.

pages.ja:
「
シロウ、これは」
セイバーの声に緊張が混じる。
……それは俺も同じだ。
無言で頷いた首筋に、冷たい汗が流れている。

pages.en:
“—Shirou, this is…”

There is tension in Saber's voice.

…I feel the same.

I nod without a word, cold sweat running down the back of my neck.

pages.ja:
……山は、それ自体が生き物のようだった。
一歩踏み出す度に走る悪寒と、息苦しいまでの圧迫感。
いや
実際、大気は濃く湿っている。

…The mountain seems to be a living creature in its own right.

Every step sends a chill through me, and the pressure is almost too great to breathe beneath.

No—the air truly is dense and damp.

…The mountain seems to be a living creature in its own right.

The wind blowing down from the temple gate is tepid, and the swaying trees resemble breathing lungs.

Every step sends a chill through me, and the pressure is almost too great to breathe beneath.

No—the air truly is dense and damp.

pages.ja:
「……魔力の密度が高い。十年前と同じです。おそらく、上ではもう」
……聖杯の召喚が始まっているか、終わったか。
どちらにせよ、ランサーはギルガメッシュに敗れたという事か。

pages.en:
“…The air holds an extraordinary concentration of Mana. It is the same as it was ten years ago. Above us, they must already have…”

…Begun the summoning of the Holy Grail—or completed it.

Either way, it must mean that Lancer was defeated by Gilgamesh.

「
確認するぞ、セイバー。
上に着いたら、あとは戦うだけだ。セイバーはギルガメッシュの相手を頼む。俺はマスター
言峰を討つ。
お互いの戦いには手を出さない。……どちらかが相手を倒せば、それで終わりだ」

言峰を討つ。
お互いの戦いには手を出さない。……どちらかが相手を倒せば、それで終わりだ」
pages.en:
“—Let's go over it one last time, Saber.

“Once we reach the top, all that remains is to fight. You take Gilgamesh. I'll defeat his Master—Kotomine.

“Neither of us interferes in the other's battle. …The moment either one of us defeats our opponent, it's over.”

pages.ja:
「ええ。今回だけは、私は自分の戦いに専念します。それに、コトミネは貴方が倒すべき敵だ」
「……そうだな。よし、任せとけ。セイバーの方こそ、あんなヤツにやられるんじゃないぞ」
pages.jaRuby:
「ええ。今回だけは、私は自分の戦いに専念します。それに、コトミネは貴方が倒すべき敵だ」
「……そうだな。よし、任せとけ。セイバーの方こそ、あんなヤツにやられるんじゃないぞ」
pages.en:
“Yes. This once, I shall devote myself entirely to my own battle. Besides, Kotomine is an enemy you must defeat yourself.”

“…Right. Leave him to me. And don't you let a bastard like that beat you, Saber.”

pages.ja: 「……はい。誇りにかけて、彼には負ける訳にはいかない。サーヴァントとしてではなく、英霊として彼の王に膝を屈する事はできません」
pages.jaRuby: 「……はい。誇りにかけて、彼には負ける訳にはいかない。サーヴァントとしてではなく、英霊として[ruby text=か]彼の王に膝を屈する事はできません」
pages.en: “…I will not. On my honor, I cannot allow him to defeat me. Not as a Servant, but as a Heroic Spirit, I will never bend the knee to that king.”

pages.ja:
強く断言するセイバーに、迷いや憂いはなかった。
なら、もう言うべき事は何もない。
俺たちは戦いに赴き、最後のマスターとして雌雄を決する。
その過程。
どちらかが命を落としても、残った一方が敵を討つだけ。

pages.en:
There is neither doubt nor sorrow in Saber's forceful declaration.

Then there is nothing more to say.

We will go to battle and, as the final Masters, decide who stands victorious.

—In the course of doing so,

if one of us loses our life, the other need only defeat the enemy.

pages.ja:
俺が倒れてもセイバーがギルガメッシュさえ倒せば、言峰は聖杯を手に入れられない。
同時に、もしセイバーが倒れたとしても
俺が言峰を倒せば、ギルガメッシュも現界していられない。
……だから、お互いを庇う必要はない。
この戦いはもう、それぞれの物に別れているのだから。

pages.en:
Even if I fall, Kotomine cannot obtain the Holy Grail so long as Saber defeats Gilgamesh.

And even if Saber falls—if I defeat Kotomine, Gilgamesh will no longer be able to remain in this world.

…Therefore, neither of us needs to protect the other.

This battle has already divided into two separate struggles.

pages.ja:
……そうして、石段を登っていく。
山門に近づけば近づくほど、空気の密度はあがっていった。
背筋に伝わる汗。
肌を刺す不吉な予感。
この石段の終わりには、お互いにとって最強の敵が待ち受けている。

pages.en:
…And so we climb the stone steps.

The nearer we draw to the mountain gate, the denser the air becomes.

Sweat trails down my spine.

A premonition of disaster needles my skin.

At the top of these stairs, the strongest enemy either of us has ever faced is waiting.

pages.ja:
だが。
そんなもの、本当はどうでも良かった。
階段を上っていく。
山門が近づいてくる。
……そうすれば、それで終わりだ。
この戦いがどちらの勝利に終わろうと、セイバーは消える。

pages.en:
—But.

In truth, none of that matters.

I keep climbing.

The mountain gate draws near.

…And once we reach it, everything will end.

Whether this battle ends in victory or defeat, Saber will disappear.

pages.ja:
長く、一瞬だった戦いの日々は終わって、セイバーはこの世界から消滅する。
彼女は本来あるべき、正しい時間に帰るのだ。
pages.jaRuby:

彼女は本来あるべき、正しい時間に帰るのだ。
pages.en:
The days of battle—so long, and over in an instant—will end, and Saber will vanish from this world.

She will return to the proper time in which she belongs.

pages.ja:
それに。
悔いがないなんて、言えるはずがない。
セイバーを失う。
守ると。幸せになってほしいと思った相手を失う。
それがどれほど辛い事か、俺はまだ知らない。
こうして共に歩いて、まだ傍らに彼女を感じられる。
失う覚悟なんて、出来ている筈がなかった。

pages.en:
—And yet.

I could never say that I have no regrets.

I am going to lose Saber.

I am going to lose the person I swore to protect, the person I wanted to be happy.

I still do not know how much that will hurt.

For now we are still walking together. I can still feel her beside me.

There is no possibility that I am prepared to lose her.

pages.ja:
何日も前に。
彼女と出会ったその日から、最後には別れがあるのだと知らされていたとしても。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en: Even though I was told, many days ago—on the very day I met her—that we would part in the end.

pages.ja:
「
」
思い返せば、数え切れない思い出があった。
共に歩いた夜もあったし、共に戦った時もあった。
初めは女の子であるセイバーに戦わせられるかと勝手に奮戦したし、道場でさんざんしごかれた。
隣りの部屋で眠るのが苦手で土蔵で眠った事もあったし、一緒に昼飯だって食べた。

“————”

Looking back, there are more memories than I could ever count.

There were nights when we walked together, and times when we fought together.

At first, I decided on my own that I could never let a girl like Saber fight and threw myself recklessly into battle. Then she put me through hell in the dojo.

I was so uncomfortable sleeping in the room beside hers that I slept in the shed instead. We even ate lunch together.

pages.ja:
セイバーは風呂が好きだったり、メシが旨いと満足そうだったり、遠坂が用意した服を気に入ったり、藤ねえとテンポの合わない会話をしてた。
無理をして、自分だけで苦労を背負いこんで、あげくに倒れて
くすんだ廃墟で、心を重ねた。

pages.en:
Saber loved the bath. She looked perfectly content whenever the food was good. She took a liking to the clothes Tohsaka prepared, and held conversations with Fuji in which neither of them ever found the other's rhythm.

She pushed herself, took every burden onto her own shoulders, and finally collapsed—and in a tarnished ruin, our hearts met.

pages.ja:
……もう、その段階でどうかしてた。
セイバーの事しか考えられなくなって、戦う目的が変わって、どうしようもなく好きなんだと気が付いた。
そんな相手を
どうやって、失えるというのだろう。

pages.en:
…By then, I had already lost all sense.

I could think of nothing but Saber. My reason for fighting changed, and I realized that I loved her beyond all hope of remedy.

How could I possibly—lose someone like that?

「
」
セイバーは何も語らない。
俺も、声をかける事ができない。
この階段が終わって、
このまま登り切ってしまえば、お互い言葉を交わす事はない。

pages.en:
“————”

Saber says nothing.

I cannot bring myself to speak to her either.

When these stairs end—

once we finish climbing them, we will exchange no more words.

pages.ja:
セイバーを失い、別れるのはまだ先だ。
けれど。
俺たちに許された別れの時間は、この瞬間しか与えられていなかった。

pages.en:
The moment when I lose Saber and we truly part lies a little farther ahead.

And yet—

this moment is the only time we have been granted in which to say goodbye.

」
……階段を登っていく。
別れを告げるのが嫌なら、なんでもないコトを、今まで通りに話せばいい。
たとえば、そう。
帰ったらもう一度町に行こう、とか。
明日の朝食は何がいい、とか。
そんな、なんでもない、コトを。

pages.en:
“————”

…We continue up the stairs.

If I do not want to bid her farewell, I could simply talk about something ordinary, the way I always have.

I could say that we should visit the city again when we return.

I could ask what she would like for breakfast tomorrow.

Something—anything—ordinary.

pages.ja:
「
」
……そんなコトさえ、口に出来ない。
何か言葉にすれば、それが別れの言葉になる。
明確な終わり。
明確なさよならを、俺もセイバーも、口にする事が出来なかった。

pages.en:
“————”

…I cannot speak even those words.

Whatever I said would become a farewell.

A definite ending.

Neither Saber nor I can bring ourselves to give voice to a definite goodbye.

pages.ja:
そうして、山門に辿り着いた。
これが最後の選択。
進めば終わる。
だが戻れば
まだ、彼女を失わないで済む方法が見つかるかもしれない。

pages.en:
—At last, we reach the mountain gate.

This is the final choice.

If we continue, it will end.

But if we turn back—perhaps we might still find some way for me not to lose her.

pages.ja:
「
セイバー」
立ち止まって、セイバーへ振り向いた。
セイバーはいつも通りだ。
平気そうな顔で、何かを堪えているような、張りつめた瞳。

pages.en:
“—Saber.”

I stop and turn toward her.

Saber looks as she always does.

Her face appears calm, while her taut eyes seem to be enduring something in silence.

pages.ja:
それを見た瞬間、ありとあらゆる誘惑が駆けめぐった。
逃げてしまえ、と。
失いたくないのなら引き返していいと。
彼女なら、おまえがそうしたいと言えば受け入れてくれると。

The moment I see them, every temptation imaginable races through me.

*Run away.*

*If you cannot bear to lose her, you may turn back.*

*If you tell her that is what you want, she will accept it.*

My resolve wavers.

The temptation rises as far as my throat.

I bite it back.

“—Let's go. This is the final battle.”

As I always have, I speak to her as her Master.

Saber nods without a word.

Her eyes are the same as ever, filled with an unyielding will.

“————”

Then I will regret nothing.

As she has placed her faith in me,

I too will believe that the choice I have made is right.

もう戻れない戦いに向かっていく。

pages.en:
We step toward the mountain gate.

We advance toward the battle from which there can be no return.

pages.en:
We could say nothing—not even what we truly wished to say.

Even so, I want to believe that this painful silence conveyed our feelings more deeply than words could have done.

それは。
まるで、遠い日の火事のように。

pages.en:
Stagnant air, saturated with the presence of death.

—It is

almost like the fire on that distant day.

赤い光に混じって、今にもあふれ出そうとしているモノがある。

“————”

But this is nothing so simple.

Something is mingled with the red light, ready to overflow at any moment.

……建物の向こう。
鮮やかな赤色に滲む、粘液のような黒い闇。
この境内が清らかな湖だとすると、あの泥はばらまかれた重油のようだ。

pages.en:
…Beyond the building,

black darkness like mucus bleeds through the brilliant red.

If these temple grounds are a clear lake, that sludge is crude oil spilled across its surface.

pages.ja:
広がり、地面を汚染し、呑み込まれたモノを殺さずにはおかない泥。
それは視覚できる程の呪いに他ならない。
俺とて魔術師のはしくれだ。
アレが、人の精神にのみ作用し、人間の体だけを飲み込むモノだと直感できる。

It spreads, polluting the earth and killing whatever it engulfs.

It is a curse made dense enough to see.

Even I am a mage of sorts.

I can tell instinctively that it acts only upon the human spirit and devours only human bodies.

来たか。待ちわびたぞ、セイバー」
その極彩色の中に、ヤツがいた。
血のような赤色も、死を帯びた黒色も知らぬと。
金色に武装したサーヴァントは、境内のただ中で俺たち
いや、セイバーを待ち受けていた。

“—So you have come. I have grown weary of waiting, Saber.”

He stands amid that riot of color.

As if the red of blood and the black of death were both beneath his notice,

the gold-armored Servant waits in the center of the temple grounds for us—no, for Saber.

pages.ja:
「頃合いも良い。聖杯もようやく重い腰をあげ、孔が開いたところだ。
この呪いこそが聖杯の中身。我らサーヴァントをこの世に留める第三要素。
十年前、おまえが我に浴びせたモノだ」

“Your timing is favorable. The Holy Grail has finally bestirred itself, and the opening has appeared.

“This curse is the substance within the Grail—the third element that anchors us Servants to this world.

“It is what you poured over me ten years ago.”

pages.ja:
ギルガメッシュはセイバーしか見ていない。
セイバーもそれは同じ。
彼女は一歩踏み込み、その剣を、目前の騎士へと向ける。
pages.jaRuby:

彼女は一歩踏み込み、その剣を、目前の騎士へと向ける。
pages.en:
Gilgamesh sees no one but Saber.

The same is true of her.

She takes one step forward and points her sword at the knight before her.

pages.ja:
「ギルガメッシュ。貴方の目的はなんだ。
あの呪い
聖杯と偽っていたモノを使って、何を望む」
pages.jaRuby:
「ギルガメッシュ。貴方の目的はなんだ。
あの呪い
聖杯と偽っていたモノを使って、何を望む」
pages.en:
“Gilgamesh. What is your purpose?

“What do you desire from that curse—from the thing that masqueraded as the Holy Grail?”

pages.ja:
「望みなどないと言っただろう。言峰が聖杯をどう扱おうと我は知らん。
今のところ、我の関心はおまえだけだ」
pages.jaRuby:
「望みなどないと言っただろう。言峰が聖杯をどう扱おうと[ruby text=オレ]我は知らん。
今のところ、[ruby text=オレ]我の関心はおまえだけだ」
pages.en:
“I told you that I desire nothing. How Kotomine elects to use the Holy Grail is no concern of mine.

“At present, you alone command my interest.”

pages.ja:
セイバーに応えるように、黄金の騎士が片腕をあげる。
同時に、ヤツの背後が陽炎と揺らぐ。
王の財宝、百を超える“宝具”が、弾丸として装填される。

pages.en:
As if responding to Saber, the golden knight raises one arm.

—At once, the air behind him shimmers like a heat haze.

The King's Treasury: more than a hundred Noble Phantasms load themselves like bullets.

pages.ja:
「……ああ、ようやくこの時が来たか。今までずっと考えていたぞセイバー。
嫌がるおまえをどう組み伏せアレを飲ませるか。
泣き噎ぶ顔を踏み付けその体を染め抜くほどの泥を飲ませ、悶え死ぬに耐えきれず我の足下にすがりつく、その穢れきった姿をな
！」

pages.en:
“…Ah, this hour has come at last. I have thought of nothing else, Saber.

“How I would force you down as you resisted and make you drink from it.

“How I would grind my heel into your sobbing face and pour enough mud down your throat to stain you through—until, unable to endure the agony of dying, you crawled to my feet in supplication. How utterly defiled you would look—!”

pages.ja:
「
よく言った。ならば、その身が同じ末路を辿ろうと異論はないな、英雄王」
さらに一歩。
無数の宝具の射程距離へと踏み込んでいくセイバー。
……それはもう、俺がどうこう出来る戦いじゃない。
セイバーとギルガメッシュの戦いは、人の身で立ち入れる物ではないのだから。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“—You have said enough. Then you will make no objection when your own body meets that same end, King of Heroes.”

One step farther.

Saber enters the range of the countless Noble Phantasms.

…This is already a battle in which I can have no part.

No human body could intrude upon the struggle between Saber and Gilgamesh.

pages.ja:
「
ふん、それでこそセイバーよ。
我には勝てないと知った上でなおその気概。宴の終わりを飾るに相応しいが
」

」
pages.en:
“—Hmph. That is precisely what makes you Saber.

“You know that you cannot defeat me, yet your spirit remains unbroken. It is a fitting ornament for the end of our banquet, but—”

pages.en: “We need no spectators. You there, mongrel—if your business is with Kotomine, be gone. He awaits you at the altar.”

！」

“——!”

Kotomine is waiting for me.

pages.ja:
……セイバーに視線を投げる。
彼女はギルガメッシュを見据えながら、わずかに頷いた。
無事を祈る、と。
その後ろ姿が告げていた。

無事を祈る、と。
その後ろ姿が告げていた。
pages.en:
…I glance toward Saber.

Without taking her eyes from Gilgamesh, she gives the slightest nod.

*I pray for your safety.*

Her back tells me all she cannot say.

pages.ja:

俺が向かう相手は他にいる。
その背後。
駆けていく背中に、死闘の開始を聞いていた。

—I turn away.

My opponent lies elsewhere.

Behind me,

as I race onward, I hear the battle to the death begin.

境内の奥。
柳洞寺の本堂の裏には、大きな池があった。
人の手は入れられず、神聖な趣きをした、龍神でも棲んでいそうな池だ。
澄んだ青色の水質は清らかで、濁りのない綺麗な池だった。

pages.en:
Deep within the grounds,

behind the main hall of Ryuudou Temple, there stood a broad pond.

Untouched by human hands, it possessed a sacred air, as though a dragon god might dwell in its depths.

Its clear blue water was pure and entirely free of cloudiness.

pages.ja:
だが、それは昨日までの話。
池は、もはや見る影もない。
目前に広がるのは赤い燐光。
黒く濁ったタールの海。
そして

pages.en:
But that was only true until yesterday.

Nothing of the pond remains as it was.

Red phosphorescence spreads before me.

A sea of black, turbid tar.

—And—

pages.ja: 中空に穿たれた『孔』と、捧げられた少女の姿。
pages.jaRuby: 中空に穿たれた『孔』と、捧げられた少女の姿。
pages.en: the “hole” bored into empty space, and the girl offered up beneath it.

「
言、峰…………！」
冷静を演じてきた思考が、一瞬にして通常値を振り切る。
駆けてきた足を止め敵を凝視する。

駆けてきた足を止め敵を凝視する。
pages.en:
“—Kotomine…………!”

In a single instant, every thought I had forced to remain calm shoots past the redline.

I stop dead and glare at my enemy.

pages.ja:
「よく来たな衛宮士郎。最後まで残った、ただ一人のマスターよ」
皮肉げに口元を歪め、ヤツは両手を広げて出迎える。
……ここが、決着の場所。
今回の聖杯戦争における、召喚の祭壇だった。

……ここが、決着の場所。
今回の聖杯戦争における、召喚の祭壇だった。
pages.en:
“Welcome, Shirou Emiya—the sole Master to survive until the end.”

His mouth twisting with irony, Kotomine spreads his arms in greeting.

…This is the place where it will be settled:

the summoning altar of the present Holy Grail War.

「
イリヤを降ろせ。おまえをぶちのめすのはその後だ」
……ヤツまでの距離は十メートルほど。
これ以上先に踏み込めば戦いが始まる。
言峰がどんな魔術師かは知らないが、おそらくは遠坂と同じ飛び道具を扱うに違いない。

“—Take Illya down. I'll beat you senseless afterward.”

…There are approximately ten meters between us.

If I advance any farther, the battle will begin.

I do not know what manner of mage Kotomine is, but he likely commands projectiles much as Tohsaka does.

“I understand your feelings, but that request is impossible. The Holy Grail has appeared, yet the opening remains unstable.

“As the point of contact, she must endure for as long as her life persists. Otherwise, my wish cannot be granted.”

For as long as her life persists—then Illya is still alive…!

“…Oh? I see. So you believe this to be the object of my desire. You truly are Kiritsugu's son.

“To think the same misunderstanding would persist for two generations.”

“What—did you say?”

pages.ja:
「この泥は私の手による物ではない。
これは聖杯より溢れる力、本来は万能である筈の“無色の力”だ。
それを黒く染めるなど人の力では出来ん。
この聖杯はな、初めからこうなのだ。開けてしまえば最後、際限なく溢れ出し災厄を巻き起こす」

「この泥は私の手による物ではない。
これは聖杯より溢れる力、本来は万能である筈の“無色の力”だ。
それを黒く染めるなど人の力では出来ん。
この聖杯はな、初めからこうなのだ。開けてしまえば最後、際限なく溢れ出し災厄を巻き起こす」
pages.en:
“This mud is not my creation.

“It is the power spilling from the Holy Grail—the ‘colorless power’ that should, by nature, be capable of anything.

“No human power could stain it black.

“This Grail was always what you see before you. Once opened, it will pour forth without end and visit calamity upon the world.”

pages.ja:
「それがこの聖杯の正体だ。
この中にはあらゆる悪性、人の世を分け隔てなく呪うモノが詰まっている。
それを操る事など、誰にも出来ん」
pages.jaRuby:
「それがこの聖杯の正体だ。

pages.en:
“That is the true nature of this Holy Grail.

“It is filled with every form of evil—with that which curses the entire human world without distinction.

“No one can control it.”

…What is that man saying?

If it is true, then he did not become a Master to fulfill some wish of his own—he did it for no reason but to open this…!?

pages.en:
“…………Kotomine. What is your wish?”

I grind my molars and glare at the black priest.

He lifts one corner of his mouth, considering.

“If I must give it a name, then let us call it entertainment.”

He delivers the answer in all its simplicity as though it were self-evident.

「
解らないのか。例えば音楽だ。歌を楽しいと思うのは何故だと思う、衛宮士郎」
「え
な、なんだって、そんな」
「では本はどうだ。物語が人を惹きつけるのは何故だと思う」
何故かって、そんな事
考えた事も、ないけど。

pages.en:
“What… did you…?”

“—Do you not understand? Consider music. Why do you suppose human beings take pleasure in song, Shirou Emiya?”

“What—why are you asking me—?”

“Then consider books. Why do stories captivate the human heart?”

Why? I have never even—thought about it.

pages.ja: 「そう、考えるまでもない。あらゆる娯楽。人間を悦ばせるモノ。それらが愉しいのは、単に人間が作った物だからだ」
pages.jaRuby: 「そう、考えるまでもない。あらゆる娯楽。人間を悦ばせるモノ。それらが愉しいのは、単に人間が作った物だからだ」
pages.en: “Precisely. It requires no thought. Every form of entertainment—everything that brings pleasure to humanity—is enjoyable for the simple reason that human beings created it.”

pages.ja: 「よいか。あらゆる創造物は人間の内より生じる物。つまるところ、この世でもっとも愉快なモノとは人間に他ならない。剥き出しの人間こそが最高の娯楽となる」
pages.jaRuby: 「よいか。あらゆる創造物は人間の内より生じる物。つまるところ、この世でもっとも愉快なモノとは人間に他ならない。[ruby text=・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・ o2o=1]剥き出しの人間こそが最高の娯楽となる」
pages.en: “Listen well. Every created thing issues from within humanity. It follows that nothing in this world is more delightful than humanity itself. *Humanity laid entirely bare* is the highest form of entertainment.”

pages.ja:
「それに比べれば、人間が生み出す娯楽など二次的なものだ。
……そう、音楽も物語も、愛憎も憐憫も信頼も裏切りも道徳も背徳も幻想も真実も……！ 全て、全て唾棄すべき不純物にすぎん。
そのようなもの、所詮は残り殻にすぎぬ二流の娯楽。
私が楽しみたいのは人間そのものでな。そのような余分なモノなど、もはや口にあわん」

pages.en:
“Compared with that, the diversions humanity creates are only derivative.

“…Music and stories. Love and hatred, compassion and trust, betrayal, virtue and vice, fantasy and truth…! All of them—every one—are contemptible impurities.

“They are nothing but spent husks, the dregs of second-rate amusements.

“What I wish to savor is humanity itself. Such unnecessary additions have long since ceased to suit my palate.”

pages.ja:
「その為には、営みなどという贅肉は削ぎ落とさなければならない。
走馬燈というものがあるだろう？ それと同じだ。人間は死の瞬間にのみ価値がある。生存という助走距離を以って高く跳び、宙に届き尊く輝くもの。その瞬きこそが私の望みだ」

pages.en:
“To reach it, one must pare away the excess flesh called human activity.

“You know the visions said to pass before one's eyes at death? It is the same principle. A human being possesses value only at the instant of death. Life is the running start from which one leaps upward, touches the heavens, and shines with sublime brilliance. That single flash is what I desire.”

pages.ja:
「それがおまえの求めた質問の答えだ。
おまえたちが平穏を糧にするように。
この身は、星の光を食べて生きている」

pages.en:
“There is the answer to your question.

“As you nourish yourselves upon tranquility,

“I sustain myself by consuming the light of stars.”

寒気がするのは、ヤツの発言にではない。
人間を愉しみたいと語るヤツそのものが、神聖な存在に見えて寒気がしたのだ。

The priest standing with his arms spread in oration is monstrous.

But it is not his declaration that chills me.

It is the sight of the man himself, speaking of his desire to enjoy humanity with the bearing of something sacred.

」

……そう、私が望むものなどその程度だ。
あのような地獄にこそ魂の炸裂、ヒトにおける最高の煌めきがある。それはおまえ自身も体験した事ではないかな衛宮士郎。
どうだ。無念のまま朽ちる人間の叫びは、胸に迫るものがあっただろう？」

“Indeed. The fire ten years ago was not without merit. It was small in scale, but filled with stimuli impossible under ordinary circumstances.

“…Yes. What I desire amounts to no more than that.

“In hells such as that, the soul erupts and humanity achieves its most brilliant radiance. You experienced it yourself, did you not, Shirou Emiya?

“Tell me. *The cries of those who perished with all their regrets upon them*—did they not *stir your heart*?”

」

あの時間が。
あの地獄が、そんな一言で。

pages.en:
“You—”

Don't… mock me.

That time—

that hell cannot be reduced to a single sentence like that.

「理解してくれたか。歪なカタチではあるが、私ほど人間を愛しているモノはいない。故に、私ほど聖杯に相応しい人間もいまい」
そうして、神父は満足そうに笑った。
あの出来事を。
為す術もなく死んでいった人たちの姿を、心の底から素晴らしいと言うかのように
！

“Now do you understand? Mine may be a distorted form of love, but no one loves humanity more deeply than I. It follows that no human being is more worthy of the Holy Grail.”

And then the priest smiles in satisfaction.

As if that event—

the sight of all those people dying helplessly—were something he admired from the bottom of his heart—!

I focus my awareness in the tips of my feet.

I gather strength in the legs that will propel me from the earth.

“—What you're saying is that I'm free to kill you…!”

There are less than ten meters between us. I will close the distance in a straight line and—

“————”

I leap sideways.

The instinct screaming that I do not want to die has overcome the reason insisting that I must kill him.

“What—was that!?”

I stare at the route I had been following a moment ago.

Something hisses as it burns the ground.

Black mud has stretched from the pond and lies there steaming.

…It resembles a black carpet.

The mud lashed like a whip to intercept me as I approached Kotomine, then fell slack and left its mark upon the earth.

“Move about as you please, but one careless step will kill you.”

っ！」

“——!”

I leap clear of the black mud reaching for me without mercy.

Careless or not, the bastard is doing everything in his power to kill me…!

“Damn—you fraudulent priest…!”

Keeping one eye upon the pond, I regain my stance.

…The distance to Kotomine remains unchanged.

Those ten meters form the line beyond which he refuses to let me advance.

…But the tendrils of mud can extend without limit. They will follow me however far I retreat, and there is no reason to think he possesses only one—

「ほう、やる気か。それは喜ばしい。
このまま立ち去るのなら殺しようがなかったが、おまえ本人が争うのであれば問題はない。
なにしろこれでも神に仕える身だ。助けを求める者を殺める訳にもいかなくてな」

“Oh? You mean to fight? How gratifying.

“Had you chosen to leave, I could hardly have killed you. But if you yourself elect to do battle, there is no difficulty.

“I remain, after all, a servant of God. I could not strike down a man who begged me for salvation.”

「
よく言う。人を背中から襲ったヤツがな、そんな言葉を吐くんじゃない」
言われて、ランサーの一件を思い出したのか。

pages.en:
“—Spare me. A man who had me attacked from behind has no right to say anything like that.”

Perhaps my words remind him of the incident with Lancer.

Kotomine smiles as though impressed.

pages.ja:
「そうだったな。おまえには、アレで愛想がつきていた。

pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“That is true. Your conduct there exhausted what little affection I had for you.

“There is no need to prolong matters further.”

「……正直に言うとな、衛宮士郎。私はおまえに期待していたのだ。凛がおまえを教会に導いた夜、運命すら感じた。おまえがあの切嗣の息子と判り、内面まで似通っていると知った時の喜びなど判るまい。
十年前に叶わなかった望み。衛宮切嗣という男に、こうしてもう一度引導を渡せるとは思わなかった」

pages.en:
“…To speak plainly, Shirou Emiya, I had expectations of you. On the night Rin brought you to the church, I felt the hand of destiny itself. You cannot imagine my delight when I discovered you were the son of that man—Kiritsugu—and that you resembled him even within.

“The desire that went unfulfilled ten years ago. I never expected to have another opportunity to deliver the final blow to the man called Kiritsugu Emiya.”

池から鎌首をあげて揺らめくそれは、黒い蛇そのものだ。

Rising and swaying from the pond, each is the perfect image of a black serpent.

Just as I thought, this is the worst possible situation.

The number of serpents continues to multiply without end.

Forget reaching Kotomine. I can no longer tell how much longer I will survive—

“Naturally, you have no prospect of victory.

“The difference between the years you have lived and those I have lived is considerable. Unless you find some means of multiplying your own, that is not a gap you can close.”

Like a conductor presiding over an orchestra, he glares into the heavens.

！」

pages.en:
“—Stake your life.

“Then perhaps you may reach me—!”

Saber slips beneath his sweeping blade and drives one step deeper into his reach—!

Every weapon he possesses conceals some unknown power. Blocking one without knowing its nature would be tantamount to suicide.

To him, this battle is nothing more than a diversion.

A struggle whose outcome was certain from the outset can inspire neither tension nor exhaustion.

Knowing it was impossible, she has continued her furious assault without conserving the least of her strength.

This is neither the first nor the second time she has driven her enemy into a corner.

And still—she has never broken through the wall of Noble Phantasms that man commands.

“You cannot defeat me, nor can he defeat Kotomine.

“You miscast the roles. Had you challenged the Holy Grail, this battle would surely have been yours.”

There is no laughter in the golden knight's eyes.

Unexpectedly, he must be speaking in earnest.

—But he is wrong.

To Saber, that choice alone would have been a mistake.

The Noble Phantasms suspended behind Gilgamesh visibly multiply.

…In truth, there is a way.

There is only one, but a means of defeating the golden knight does exist.

*—But for it to work—*

*—Endure Ea…? Impossible. Even with the scabbard returned to me, one blow from that weapon would leave me unable to rise.*

But there is no other path to victory.

How can she draw that slender thread toward herself and spin it into possibility?

The probability of victory must be so slight that the possibility of reversal does not yet exist.

Without Gilgamesh touching them, the weapons stir and turn themselves toward Saber one after another.

Those that had revealed only their hilts now bare their blades and await their master's command.

Gilgamesh was never a swordsman.

These countless Noble Phantasms deploy themselves through space and, at their master's command, become projectiles in their own right.

That is why his class is Archer.

This Servant is the marksman who commands the mightiest barrage of magical projectiles.

Her armor shatters. Her gauntlets are pierced. Even the garments protecting her feet are skewered.

Even in those desperate straits, Saber avoids every mortal wound—and then sees the worst possible sight.

The instant her feet touch earth, she drives magical energy into the holy sword.

Scattering his own Noble Phantasms before him, Gilgamesh completes a single stroke of Ea, the Sword of Rupture—

I tear away the slime clinging to my ankle.

My clothing hisses as it burns, leaving the skin beneath exposed.

“Gh—ah!”

I leap back from a descending tendril.

There is no feeling in my right ankle where the slime adhered. I cannot even tell whether my foot remains attached below the heel, but I hurl myself into the open ground ahead all the same.

I inspect my body as I roll.

My ankle. Good, the foot is still there. It has only lost all sensation. So long as it remains attached, I should still be able to run somehow.

The smell of earth burning makes my head reel. I force my thoughts together, rise, and then—

“Gh————!”

Blazing heat tears across my back.

“You—bastard—!”

I fling it away and leap toward an empty patch of ground.

Perhaps that ended the pursuit.

For the moment, none of the black mud that had writhed all around me remains within sight—

…I bite my lip.

After all that running,

I have only been driven back here.

“Hah—hah, hah, ha—”

I steady my breathing and glare at him, refusing to let him defeat me in spirit if nothing else.

…Kotomine has not moved a single step. He merely stands in the same place and watches me flee for my life.

もう限界だ、休ませろ、おまえが休ませないなら俺が出ていくとばかりに、喉から這い上がってきそうな勢い。

“Hah… hah, hah, hah, hah—”

…No matter how deeply I breathe, my heart will not calm.

It seems ready to crawl out through my throat, protesting that it has reached its limit, demanding rest—and threatening to abandon me if I refuse.

There is nothing I can do.

I cannot approach Kotomine, and I cannot silence the black mud.

…Nor am I holding Projection in reserve as some final hope.

That blade could tear through this black mud and carry me straight to Kotomine.

“Hah—ah, gh—!?”

“Gh—!”

I throw my head back and evade the mud by a hair.

…A single tendril is not especially formidable.

It moves more slowly than Saber's shinai and strikes only the place it aims for with perfect honesty. Dodging it is easy.

pages.ja:
だがそれも一本だけの話。
何十という泥、躱した瞬間に背中に落ちてくるものまでは対処しきれない。
結果として動き回るしかなく、その間にも少しずつ体は泥で汚れていく。

I cannot cope with dozens of them, least of all those that descend behind me the instant I evade another.

I have no choice but to keep moving, and all the while the mud stains my body little by little.

そんな隙を見せれば、俺はとっくに骨になっている。

“Hah—you damned—!”

There is not a moment to rest.

I cannot perform Projection under these conditions.

Building the image of a weapon from nothing demands almost a full minute of uninterrupted concentration, even at its fastest.

If I left myself open for that long, I would already be nothing but bones.

“Hah—hah, hah, hah, ah—!”

Every joint and every patch of flesh touched by the mud after I failed to evade it has lost all feeling.

The absence of pain is my one mercy. But when this spreads over my whole body, I will no longer be able to tell whether I am alive or dead.

That will be the end. More than that—by then, the mud will have dissolved me without leaving even my bones.

I can only run.

I know it is merely a matter of time before my strength gives out, but for now, all I can do is run.

There is no possibility that blind fortune will carry me closer to Kotomine as I evade the black mud.

On the contrary, I cannot approach him now. Behind the man, the mud descends in a veritable waterfall.

…I am still conscious.

Mud coils around my wrist and throat like chains, but some feeling remains in my body.

“I shall end it soon enough. But doing so immediately would lack artistry. You are Kiritsugu's counterfeit. The debt he incurred ten years ago will be repaid with your death.”

I clench my teeth against it and inspect my right leg.

…The verdict is black.

It neither feels nor moves. I must either expel the mud staining my body or pour magical energy into the leg and force out the congealed blood.

…Either way, the instant I make it move, every muscle in my right leg will tear apart.
